summary.text: Penny Brown Reynolds, a Democrat, won the November 3, 2026 election for Georgia Secretary of State, defeating Tim Fleming, according to unofficial results, and is set to take office when the new term begins.
She is an attorney and former judge of the State Court of Fulton County who also worked in the U.S. Department of Agriculture during the Biden administration.

paragraphs.text: Reynolds earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice in 1991 and a law degree in 1994 from Georgia State University, a master's degree from the Interdenominational Theological Center in 2008, and a Ph.D. in criminal justice from Nova Southeastern University in 2021.
Reynolds was a lawyer to Roy Barnes, Georgia's last Democratic governor, and served as a judge of the State Court of Fulton County.
She hosted the nationally syndicated television program Family Court with Judge Penny and served as Acting Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights at the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
She announced her campaign for Secretary of State in September 2025 and won the Democratic nomination in the June 16, 2026 runoff.
Penny Brown Reynolds won the November 3, 2026 general election for secretary of state with 55.7% of the vote to Tim Fleming's 44.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
